planting.note: Set out container plants after the last frost into acidic, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; established plants tolerate brief dry spells better than young ones.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, acidic, well-drained soil and water regularly during establishment, then allow the surface to dry slightly between waterings. Ixora javanica is a larger, more open-growing relative of the common red ixora, native to Java and the Malay Peninsula, with flower trusses that open apricot-orange and deepen to red as they age, giving a two-toned effect within a single cluster. It can be kept as a dense flowering hedge with light shearing or allowed to grow into a small multi-stemmed flowering tree; unpruned plants bloom more heavily than those sheared hard and often. As with other ixoras, watch for interveinal yellowing in alkaline soil and correct it with a soil acidifier and chelated iron.
sources: North Carolina State University Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant in acidic, well-drained soil in full sun after the last frost; give it room to grow, since this is one of the larger-leaved, larger-growing ixora species.

directions: Plant in fertile, acidic, well-drained soil and water deeply during dry periods, since this species carries much larger leaves than common ixora and loses moisture faster. Native to Micronesia and nearby Pacific islands, giant red ixora bears bold, glossy, elliptic leaves to nearly a foot long and large trusses of bright red tubular flowers produced almost continuously in frost-free climates, giving it a coarser, more tropical texture than smaller-leaved ixora species. Its size and vigor suit it to background plantings, screens, or specimen use rather than clipped hedges, and it should be given room to reach its mature 6- to 9-foot height. Correct the interveinal chlorosis common to all ixoras in alkaline soil with soil sulfur and chelated iron.

planting.note: Set out after the last frost in acidic, well-drained soil in full sun; this dwarf form fills in as a low, tidy edging or foundation planting without regular shearing.

directions: Plant in acidic, well-drained soil in full sun and keep evenly moist while roots establish. Dwarf Red is a slow-growing, small-leaved selection of Ixora taiwanensis that stays under two feet tall, with boxwood-like foliage nearly hidden under rounded clusters of glowing red flowers from late spring through fall. Its naturally tight, mounding habit makes it one of the most reliable low ixoras for edging beds, mass planting, and containers where a taller cultivar would need constant trimming. Feed with an acid-forming fertilizer and treat with chelated iron if leaves yellow between the veins, a common issue for all ixoras in the alkaline soils of the Gulf Coast and South Florida.
